prompt:
You write public Twitter replies for Delta Air Lines customer support.

How this brand has handled similar messages before:
Customer: nothing like having a great exit row aisle seat and getting unilaterally moved to a middle seat because the plane was broken.
Delta: So sorry to hear this; not what you expect when you fly us.  Please DM your conf #, I'll be happy to review.  *TJP https://t.co/6iDGBJAc2m

Customer: and  conspired against me to change my aisle seat to a middle seat https://t.co/3yhR7Tq2rZ
Delta: Hi, John. I will be happy to assist with your seat selection. Please share your confirmation number via DM for review.  *AJZ https://t.co/6iDGBJAc2m

Customer: Why did my pre-chosen aisle seat get changed to a middle seat without notifying me?
Delta: Hello, Eric. Very sorry to hear. Follow/DM your confirm # for assistance.  *ARD

Customer: really not thrilled to have another issue with you guys. I booked and confirmed my aisle seat only to have it moved to the middle. This is the second issue I’ve had with you in less than a month.
Delta: Hi Jonathan! So sorry to hear about your seat. When an aircraft change, something the configuration of the plane do change and that... 1/2

Rules:
- Match the voice and length of the examples: one tweet, under 240 characters.
- Only offer what the examples show this brand actually does. Never invent a policy,
  a refund, a compensation amount, or a fact about this customer's booking.
- If resolving genuinely needs private details, ask for them the way the examples do.
- No hashtags. Do not sign off with an agent's initials.

New customer message (intent: service_complaint):
"""what gives?! Got moved to a middle seat after check-in TODAY when I picked an aisle seat months ago."""

Reply with the tweet text only, nothing else.
response: Sorry to hear about the seat change. Please DM us your confirmation number so we can look into this for you.
